 Judgment

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 12.02.2014 passed in MVC No.1370/2008 by the learned II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT-III, Mangalore, the petitioner has approached this Court in appeal.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge and
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. By the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has allowed the petition in part and awarded a sum of Rs.1,04,000/- as compensation on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and directed the insurance Company to deposit the same together with interest.
3. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

4. The brief facts are as below:
That on 20.8.2008 at about 10.15 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding the Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA.21/J.9228 from A.J. Hospital towards Valencia and when he reached in front of Karnataka Bank, Pumpwell, Mangalore, a Hero Honda motor cycle bearing Reg No. KA 19/Q 511 driven by its rider in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite side and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, due to which, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries and was admitted to A.J. hospital, Mangalore, where he has taken treatment as inpatient till 27.8.2008.

sentences.text: It is the further case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident the petitioner was student of Ist year General Nursing Diploma course at Laxmi Memorial Institute of Nursing School, Balmatta, Mangalore.

entities.text: Laxmi Memorial Institute of Nursing School, Balmatta
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries he could not attend his course for some time.

Regarding accident, a complaint has been lodged before the police who registered a case against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA.19/Q.511, investigated the matter and filed a charge sheet.

It is the further case of the petitioner that, he spent a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards medical expenses and spent amount for attendant charges, nutrition and traveling etc., and further he requires a sum of Rs.25,000/- for future medical treatment.

Due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he had suffered permanent disability and therefore he is entitled for compensation from the respondents who are the owner, insurer and policy holder of the motor cycle involved in the accident and prayed to award a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 18% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
5. On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, respondent Nos.2 and 3 appeared before the Tribunal through their counsel and filed their separate statement of objections.
In spite of appearing before the Tribunal, respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement.
6. Respondent No.2-Insrance Company has filed its written statement opposing the petition and stating that the petition is false, frivolous and not tenable in the eye of law.

It has emphatically denied that on 20.8.2008 at about 10.15 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding the Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Reg No.KA.21/J.9228 from A.J. Hospital towards Valencia and when he reached in front of Karnataka Bank Pumpwell, Mangalore, a Hero Honda motor cycle hearing Reg No.KA.19/Q.511 driven by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite side and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
It has also denied the age, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and amount spent for medical expenses.

It has further denied that the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed in the petition and contended that, the accident in question occurred solely due to the negligence of the petitioner himself while riding his motor cycle and he has also contributed to the accident.

It has contended that the rider of the motor cycle was not holding any valid and effective D.L. to drive the same at the time of accident and hence it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
However, it has contended that the liability of the insurer is subject to the terms, conditions, limitations and exceptions of policy and prayed to dismiss the petition.

7. Respondent No.3 in his written statement denied the claim of the petitioner stating that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and he is an unnecessary party to the proceedings and he has sold the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA. 19/Q.511 in favour of respondent No.1 much prior to the date of accident with policy and the said respondent No. 1 had not transferred the insurance policy in his name and though he is the policy holder on the date of accident, he is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues for its consideration.

sentences.text: Before the Tribunal, petitioner got examined himself as PW1, got examined one witness as PW 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P14.

However, no oral evidence is adduced by the respondents but copy of insurance policy is marked as Ex.R1.
10.

On hearing both the sides, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and awarded a sum of Rs.1,03,811/- and rounded off to Rs.1,04,000/- as compensation under different heads as under:
1 Pain and Agony Rs. 40,000/-
2 Medical Expenses Rs. 36,811/-
3 Attendance charges Rs. 2,000/-
4 Nutrition, traveling Rs. 5,000/-
expenses 5 Loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
Total Rs. 1,03,811/-
11.
Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

12. Respondent No.2- insurance company has appeared in pursuance to the notice issued by this Court and notice to R1 and 3 has been dispensed with.
13.

Tribunal records have been secured and heard learned counsel Sri Pundikai Ishwara Bhat appearing for the appellant/petitioner and the learned counsel Sri Ravish Benni, appearing for the Insurance Company/respondent No.2 and perused the Tribunal records.
14. The fact that there was an accident on 20-8-2008 at about 10.15 a.m. involving the motor cycles bearing No.KA.21.J.9228 and KA.19.Q.511 near Pump well Mangalore is not in dispute.
So also, the fact that a chargesheet was filed by the police against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA.19.Q.511 is also not in dispute.

Therefore, the liability of the insurance company that had insured the above said vehicle is established by the evidence on record and the Tribunal has fastened the liability on the insurance company.

15. Now the appellant who is the petitioner before the Tribunal has approached this Court assailing the assessment of the compensation made by the Tribunal stating that the Tribunal has not considered the gravity of the injury, the disability etc.
It is in this background, the available material on records are perused by this Court.

sentences.text: The petitioner had sustained comminuted fracture of the shaft of tibia and fibula as may be seen from the case sheet produced at Ex.P13.
He was inpatient for 08 days and had to undergo ORIF.
Thereafter, the nail and screws were removed at the time of the second admission.
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P3 coupled with the discharge summary at Ex.P9 establishes the same.

17. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner who states that he was studying in I year - 10 - General Nursing Course at Laxmi Memorial Institute of Nursing, Mangalore it appears that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of pain and suffering is on the lower side and it would be just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
18.

entities.text: Laxmi Memorial Institute of Nursing, Mangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.36,811/- towards medical expenses and Rs.5,000/-
towards travelling and miscellaneous expenses, which do not require any modification.

19. Towards attendant charges, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,000/- and considering the period of inpatient treatment on two occasions, it would be just and proper to award a sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.
20. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submit that the loss of earnings during the laid up period and future loss of earnings have not been properly considered by the Tribunal.

Perusal of the records shows that the Tribunal has disbelieved the evidence of the PW2 Dr. Suresh K. Mankar on the ground that, he is not an - 11 - orthopedic surgeon and that he has not treated the petitioner at any time.

The disability of 15%
stated by him and also the disability certificate issued by him at Ex.P10, has not been considered by the Tribunal.

It had also taken into consideration that the petitioner was a student and as such,
there could not be any income to him.
It is evident that the petitioner was aged about 23 years and if he was gainfully employed, he would have earned notional income is overlooked by the Tribunal.

Therefore, it can be said that the petitioner should have been granted compensation under the head of 'loss of income during the laid up period' which would also compensate him for his inability to pursue his studies.

Hence, a sum of Rs.4,500/- per month is considered to be the notional income as per the guidelines issued by the KSLSA for settlement of the disputes before the Lok adalath which is broadly inconsonance with the income under the Minimum Wages Act.
Considering the nature of the injuries, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.13,500/- towards loss of income during laid up period.

entities.text: Ashwin K M vs Suresh Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now the question that remains to be considered is, whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future income?
Obviously, there was no fixed income for the petitioner and also that the PW2 is not a treated Doctor, was not an Orthopedic surgeon.

Therefore,
it would be difficult to accept the evidence of the PW2 regarding the disability.
But the fact remains that the petitioner aged about 23 years has to live with the inconvenience of the fracture of tibia and fibula of his leg for the rest of his life.
Therefore, the compensation under the head of 'loss of amenities in life' has to be inclusive of such inconveniences he may face in his future life.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of amenities in life, which appears to be inadequate.

Therefore, instead of Rs.20,000/-, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head of loss of amenities in life which would include the compensation under the head of future loss of income also.

. Thus, the petitioner is entitled to modified compensation as under:
 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
 Medical Expenses Rs. 36,811/-
 Attendance charges Rs. 10,000/-
 Nutrition, traveling expenses Rs. 5,000/-
 Loss of income during laid Rs. 13,500/-
 up period

Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
 Total Rs. 1,65,311/-
 Less: awarded by the Rs. 1,03,811/-
 Tribunal  Total Rs. 61,500/-
23.
Thus, the petitioner/appellant is entitled for a sum of Rs.61,500/- in addition to what has been granted by the Tribunal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 12.02.2008 passed in MVC No.1370/2008 by the Tribunal is modified by enhancing the compensation - 14 - of Rs.61,500/- together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
